subject: VPC fee alignment and SLA risk-share request
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@cloudhealthz.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: CloudHealthz Procurement <procurement@cloudhealthz.com>
Date: 2025-10-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: VPC commercial model + surge handling (RFP attached)
Attachments: CloudHealthz_RFP_202510.pdf (pdf), CHZ_expected_QPS.xlsx (xlsx)

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudHealthz liked the latency profile and the KV-caching approach. We're starting to put together a formal procurement packet and I wanted to get clarity on two things before we share the RFP with legal:

1) How does Redwood split the platform fee versus operator license in a private VPC/on-prem setup? Our finance team wants to understand amortization for the platform fee vs per-operator line items.

2) Surge/burst credits: during product launches we expect short multi-hour spikes (50–200% over baseline). Can you outline options for surge credits or burst capacity pricing rather than forcing us into a large fixed reserve?

I've attached a rough QPS forecast (CHZ_expected_QPS.xlsx) and the RFP draft — procurement wants numbers we can include in the evaluation. We're targeting a vendor decision by Oct 20 and would need a pilot agreement + SOW that covers a 30–60 day PoC.

If helpful we can do a 30-minute call for the commercial walkthrough. Appreciate any early guidance.

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudHealthz

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@cloudhealthz.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-06T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC commercial model + surge handling (RFP attached)

Elaine — thanks for the RFP and the forecast. Quick notes up front, and I can follow up with a formal pricing sheet (RDW_pricing_options.xlsx).

- Platform fee: typically amortized monthly across the committed term; for private deployments we offer two treatments: (a) fully amortized platform fee (lower monthly but non-refundable), or (b) smaller platform fee + higher operator licenses. We can show the P&L impact side-by-side for both.
- Operator license: per-seat/per-operator or per-site operator SKUs depending on how you structure SRE responsibilities. We can make operator licenses transferrable between named operators within the same account.
- Surge credits: three approaches we commonly use:
  • Burst credits (metered): you pre-buy a bucket of burst credits that are consumed during spikes — lower up-front commitment, pay-as-consumed beyond bucket.
  • Dynamic bursting with on-demand pricing: no pre-buy, higher per-hour surcharge during spikes (good for unpredictable events).
  • Hybrid reserve + surge discount: smaller reserve for steady-state with a capped surge surcharge above threshold.

Action items for us: can you confirm a typical peak window length (hours) and the percentage of traffic above baseline you expect? That will let us map your forecast to burst credit sizing and show numeric examples.

I'll loop in Marissa and Monica to prepare three concrete commercial constructs (pilot, blended commit, fixed reserve) with support tiers and SLO language.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@cloudhealthz.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-07T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC commercial model + surge handling (RFP attached)

Elaine / Rishi — looping in a short commercial playbook so procurement has concrete options. Attached is an editable workbook (RDW_pricing_options.xlsx). High level options: 

Option A — Pilot / Proof of Value (recommended first step)\- Term: 60 days\- Platform fee: waived for pilot (pilot credit)\- Operator licenses: trial-count at no charge up to 5 operators\- Surge: metered on-demand pricing; 200% surcharge above agreed pilot baseline\- Support: Standard SRE onboarding (email + 4hr response), 1 workshop included\- Outcome: production-ready SOW to convert to Option B or C

Option B — Blended Commitment (most common for scaleups)\- Term: 12 months\- Platform fee: amortized monthly (lower monthly number)\- Operator license: per-operator monthly at discounted rate\- Surge: burst credits bucket sized to your QPS forecast + 25% safety margin; additional consumption billed at discounted surge rate\- Support: Priority SRE + 1x/month health checks, 24/7 escalation for critical incidents

Option C — Fixed Reserve (enterprise predictable)\- Term: 24–36 months\- Platform fee: higher upfront amortization protection + exit protection clause\- Operator license: site license option (flat)\- Surge: included up to a defined % above baseline (e.g., 50%), large bursts handled via negotiated credits or engineering assistance windows\- Support: Dedicated named SRE, runbook co-development, SLA credits for missed targets

Notes / asks for sizing: we used your CHZ_expected_QPS.xlsx to size burst buckets; can you confirm the payroll windows when launches occur and whether those will be global or US-only? Also procurement asked for SOC2 evidence and a template SOW — we've got a draft SOW (SOW_pilot_draft.docx) and will include our SOC2 attestations link in the packet.

Next steps: do you want to take Option A pilot and then move to B, or prefer to skip pilot and go straight to a blended commit? I'm happy to set a pricing call tomorrow or Friday.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Jim O'Neal <jim.oneal@cloudhealthz.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@cloudhealthz.com>, procurement@cloudhealthz.com
Date: 2025-10-08T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC commercial model + surge handling (RFP attached)

Marissa / Rishi — thanks for the clear options. Procurement reviewed and has a few asks / redlines before we can proceed to a pilot PO: 

1) Pilot credits: procurement wants an explicit commitment that the pilot credits will convert to a credit on the first production invoice if we sign a purchase order within 90 days.
2) SLA risk-share: for Option B they want a capped service credit schedule tied to incident severity (we'll share a template).
3) SOC2 and data residency: need a pointer to the SOC2 report and confirmation that all logs for the private deployment will remain in our AWS account (we'll need a short schedule describing telemetry retention).

Attached: CloudHealthz_RFP_202510.pdf (we included our procurement template). If you can accept #1 and provide the SOC2 pointer, procurement can issue a pilot PO within 48–72 hours.

Regards,
Jim O'Neal
VP, Infrastructure Operations
CloudHealthz

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: VPC commercial model + surge handling (RFP attached)

Jim / Elaine — appreciate the clarity. We can accept procurement ask #1: pilot credit converts to a production invoice credit if you execute a PO within 90 days — we'll add that language to the pilot SOW.

On SOC2 and telemetry: here's a private link to our SOC2 Type II attestations and evidence summary (we will include the full report under NDA): https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-2025 (we'll also provide a short telemetry schedule confirming logs remain in your AWS account for the private deployment, retention default 90 days configurable).

I'll have Marissa and Monica pull the pilot SOW with that 90-day conversion clause and return a DocuSign packet for signature. Proposed next step: sign pilot PO, kick off a 60-day pilot with a scoped runbook and two joint runbook workshops.

I'll create the RDW deal record and mark Deal ID RDW-2025-CHZ-091. Expect the pilot SOW doc back by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks — look forward to getting this started.
Rishi
